newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says portfolio investments surge in H1.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says portfolio investments surge in H1.

text.p: Net portfolio investments in Turkey showed a provisional $3.59 billion surplus in the first half 1996, in sharp contrast to a $588 million deficit in the same 1995 period, the central bank said.

The Turkish Treasury secured a total of $1.89 billion from international markets via Euroyen, Samurai, Euromark, Eurodollar bond issues and repaid $495 million in the first half, compared to $255 million secured and $1.1 billion repaid in January-June 1995.
A net influx of $2.19 billion was due to sale of foreign securities abroad by people living in Turkey, up sharply from $259 million in first half 1995.

Turkey's capital flow had shown a $4.72 billion surplus last year after a $4.19 billion deficit in 1994.
But the 1995 current account deficit was $2.34 billion, in sharp contrast to a $2.63 billion surplus in the previous year.

First half current account balance is not yet available as foreign trade statistics are delayed due to technical problems caused by Turkey's customs union with the European Union which went into effect in January.
